reason: The portal vessel fits the digestive tube's named empty slot and connects the intestine to the liver.
expectation: The vessel should complete the gut-to-liver connection in the digestive model.

effect: The portal vessel is fitted, completing the digestive tube's listed slots.
reason: The liver tissue is positioned to receive the glucose and amino acids in portal blood.
expectation: The nutrients should reach the liver tissue, allowing glucose handling to be examined.

effect: Portal nutrients now flow past liver cells, setting up the glucose-storage step.
reaction: The route from intestine to liver is clear.
reason: Glycogen-making enzymes should let the liver store some of the arriving glucose.
expectation: Liver cells will link glucose into glycogen for storage.

effect: The liver now stores glucose as glycogen, setting up the release step.
reaction: The branching granules make the storage form clear.
reason: The glycogen-release enzymes should show how stored glucose becomes available again.
expectation: The liver will break down glycogen to release glucose.

effect: The liver is now releasing glucose from stored glycogen; blood transport may carry it onward.
reason: Blood transport is the remaining component for carrying glucose away from the liver.
expectation: Glucose released by the liver will enter blood travelling away from it.

effect: Glucose is now carried away from the liver in blood, completing the storage-and-release goal.
reaction: The connection to supplying other tissues is clear.
reason: The fitted digestive tube and integrated body model are the remaining major systems to connect.
expectation: The digestive system should join the body's circulation and other connected systems.

effect: The digestive organs are now connected to the body's blood vessels, nerves and lymph routes, completing the chapter.
reaction: The final integration is satisfying, though the picture description leaves the individual connections fairly general.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following glucose from portal blood into glycogen storage and back into blood was most worthwhile: the sequence gives the liver's connection to the intestine a functional purpose.

leastWorthwhile.text: The separate release and blood-transport steps felt somewhat repetitive; the picture of release already suggested glucose leaving the liver cell.

surprise.text: The final integration also connects the digestive organs to nerves and lymph routes, not just blood vessels, although it does not detail those connections.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless, though making blood transport a separate component after glucose release felt a little mechanical.

continue.text: I would choose to continue if another chapter developed the system connections in more detail; tracing a concrete process through the constructions was more interesting than simply fitting organs together.
